newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFins slip in profit-taking,trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins slip in profit-taking,trend unclear.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds slipped in profit-taking after strong gains last week, and dealers were mixed on where the market would go in the next few days.
They said market direction was difficult to forecast as tranches 3 and 7 were mostly out of circulation, seriously diminishing market volume.
"There was slight profit-taking mainly in the fifth tranche, primarily by Western operators," a Russian dealer said.
He forecast a slight downward trend in the next few days, adding that he expected tranche 3 to fall by 0.5 percent at most and the other tranches to slip by one percent.
He said investors preferred to hold tranche 3, which gave a healthy eight-percent yield, to maturity, making price changes in the shortest paper insignificant.
A Western dealer said operators would hold tranche 7 in their portfolios for a while as the paper gave 10.5 percent yield to maturity.
He said the market would remain quiet in the next few days but forecasts an imminent rise as MinFins lagged other emerging markets debt.
Dealers said news Standard & Poor's would revise Russia's credit rating fairly soon this year did not affect the market.
"This is already priced-in," the Western dealer said.
